summary.headline: Kilburn Q2 FY27 console revenue flat YoY at ₹153.1 crore; standalone PAT fell to ₹5.7 crore on customer deferrals, subsidiaries carried the group.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 revenue was ₹153.1 crore, flat against ₹153.6 crore a year earlier and up 30.9% QoQ, with consolidated PAT of ₹16.5 crore. H1 consolidated revenue fell 4.5% to ₹270.1 crore, while subsidiaries (NGA Energy and Monga Strafil) roughly doubled revenue to ₹141.7 crore and now exceed half of group revenue. Standalone Q2 revenue dropped to ₹69.5 crore from ₹114.8 crore and PAT to ₹5.7 crore from ₹18 crore, which management attributes to customer deferrals linked to geopolitical uncertainty. Management cut FY27 group revenue expectations to ₹600-650 crore and is reiterating a 20-25% CAGR target from FY26 to FY28 and a ~20% margin.

financial_highlights.change: Roughly doubled from ₹73.4 crore in H1 FY26; contribution and profit contribution both up 21%
Management attributed decline to product mix and higher employee cost and value of raw materials consumed
vs ₹485 crore at start of quarter, after executing ₹151 crore in Q2

segments.name: Standalone (Kilburn Engineering)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹69.5 crore (vs ₹114.8 crore) and PAT ₹5.7 crore (vs ₹18 crore). Management says decline is timing-related; customers in export and capital goods deferred finalisation and dispatch. Q2 new orders ₹136 crore, led by fertilisers, carbon black and AI data centres.

segments.name: NGA Energy (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue acquired at about ₹70 crore; management targets capacity supporting over ₹300 crore theoretical capacity post Phase 2 in Pune, and says the two subsidiaries together can deliver over ₹500 crore subject to orders in FY28. Entering ferro alloy and steel WHR platforms and a cement WHR qualification.

segments.name: Monga Strafil (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue base ~₹70-80 crore at acquisition; capacity to scale to over ₹200 crore from ₹100 crore base including RF业务. Data centre enclosures expected to reach ~₹100 crore revenue in FY28; ₹25 crore capex at Pune to add capacity over 6-9 months, with capacity additions from January.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group revenue expected at ₹600-650 crore; management said Q4 could move this range materially depending on order finalisation timing.
Standalone FY27 revenue indicated around ₹700 crore in one response, later framed as indicative and subject to change.

Targeting 20-25% revenue CAGR over FY26-FY28 (FY28 revenue ₹900-2,000 crore cited in one answer; analyst derived ₹850-900 crore), with a blended EBITDA margin around 20% long term; no quarterly margin guidance.
Standalone order intake target around ₹800 crore for FY27; ₹300+ crore booked to date, with ~₹200-250 crore of opportunities expected to close in 45-60 days.
Group ambition to become a ₹1,000 crore company in a couple of years; group manufacturing infrastructure to support over ₹1,000 crore annual revenue.
Standalone capex of ~₹25 crore at Kilburn to be commissioned by December; data centre capex ₹25 crore to complete in 6-9 months.
Operating cash flow expected to remain negative for FY27, with reduction but year-end debtor build-up.
capex_capacity: Brownfield expansion at Kilburn's Raleigh (Rajkot/unspecified) plant and NGA Energy Phase 2 in Pune due for completion by Q3 to early Q4 FY27; civil works largely complete per management and equipment being commissioned.

Board approved ₹25 crore investment mainly at Monga Strafil Pune facility for enclosures, cabinets and engineered assemblies for data centres, transformers and BESS; to be implemented over 6-9 months, with added capacity from January and full capacity in first half of FY28.
Kilburn standalone capex of about ₹25 crore to be commissioned by December 2026 (Umbarnath and Raleigh plants referenced).
Management said standalone could reach ₹750-800 crore with current plants if order book is strong, including bought-out components.
Management said order-book conversion is not constrained by factory capacity; NGA capacity could extend beyond ₹350-400 crore with more EPC orders.
demand_pricing: Standalone order book ₹471 crore at 30 Sep 2026, versus ₹485 crore at start of quarter; Q2 execution ₹151 crore.
Q2 order wins ₹136 crore across fertilisers, carbon black and AI data centres; order book spread across fertilisers, carbon black, iron and steel and nuclear power.
Entry into global fertiliser ecosystem with multiple inquiries; ferro alloy entry via a Mutan order; cement WHR qualification.
Data centre enclosures: Vertiv (long-standing customer) indicated ~₹90 crore requirement in FY27; management says demand exceeds current supply and it supplies max-outs to all customers.
Management said contracts generally have no price escalation clause; raw materials are procured quickly after order award to protect margins.
Management said a portion of receivables exceed 120 days and some exceed 180 days, tied to customer commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: What exactly are the data centre enclosures, who are the competitors, and does precision engineering extend beyond data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Enclosures are customised metal cabinets housing servers and networking/power hardware for data centres; certifications are a barrier. Management is not aware of listed competitors. Current work is limited to power transformers and data centres; no aerospace mention.

qa_highlights.question: Current order pipeline versus the ₹800 crore FY27 intake expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: ₹300+ crore booked YTD; ₹800 crore is the FY27 order intake target, and closing order book should be higher than ₹471 crore by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Expected standalone revenue and whether FY27 can match FY26 top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management indicated ₹600-650 crore group revenue and around ₹700 crore standalone; subsidiaries expected to contribute more; FY26 base around ₹620 crore; range can change in Q4 on order timing.

qa_highlights.question: Data centre order size, customer count and ramp timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name other customers or order sizes; said revenue from the segment should rise over the next 4-8 quarters after capex; precision engineering to cross ₹100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Group capacity and utilisation; operating leverage and margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: NGA Phase 2 theoretical capacity above ₹300 crore; Monga Strafil scaling to over ₹200 crore; together over ₹500 crore subject to orders in FY28. Margin guidance remains a blended ~20%; no quarterly margin guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated EBITDA margin fall to 16.5% and what drove costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Combination of product mix and higher employee cost, plus a higher share of raw material value consumed (not raw material price escalation).

qa_highlights.question: Operating cash flow and receivables ageing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash flow to stay negative for FY27 though lower; year-end billing builds debtors; some receivables over 120 days and some over 180 days.

risks_watch: Standalone order conversion: ~₹200-250 crore of orders (Middle East via a newly formed JV, Far East, domestic nuclear) expected in 45-70 days; slippage would pressure FY27 revenue and FY28 ramp.
Guidance credibility: FY27 revenue guidance was cut to ₹600-650 crore from a prior ~₹775 crore per analyst; management says Q4 could move substantially.
Margin pressure: consolidated EBITDA margin 16.5% in Q2; H2 needs ~22-23% to reach ~20% full-year per analyst math; management declined to commit to a quarterly figure.
Negative operating cash flow with receivables over 120 and 180 days; no ageing percentage disclosed.
Data centre ramp dependent on a few customers (Vertiv named); capex ₹25 crore due in 6-9 months; ₹90 crore Vertiv requirement is indicative only.
Promoter pledge of about 5 lakh shares (less than 1% of promoter holding) created around Sep/Oct 2026 for an entity-level requirement; management said it will inform any change.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the group and long-term targets but defensive on near-term numbers: management repeatedly called the standalone weakness timing-related and declined to guide quarterly margins, while giving revenue ranges that were revised during the call.
key_quotes: I would like to start saying that the standalone performance was more of a timing issue than a structural one.
There has been no structural change in our business.
But we believe that this year would now look more like a transition year, a year of consolidation and a lot of the work being put in by the management will refloat in FI 28.
